messages:
emma_support: Pushing up a customer escalation — console filters not applying when selecting region=eu and model version=1.2. Dashboard still shows global totals, customer seeing billing spike. anyone? :frowning:

mike_prod: can you paste repro steps + a screenshot? also org id and a sample network request if possible

emma_support: repro steps:
1) Console -> Analytics -> Requests
2) Filters: Region = eu-west-1, Model = 'rw-bert-large', Version = 1.2
3) Time range = last 24h
expected: charts scoped to EU only. actual: global totals
URL: https://console.redwood.ai/analytics?region=eu-west-1&model=rw-bert-large&version=1.2
(screenshot attached in thread but not included here)

jordan_console: i can repro locally. network payload from the UI looks like:
```json
{
  "filters": [
    {"key": "region", "value": "eu-west-1"},
    {"key": "model_version", "value": "1.2"}
  ]
}
```
backend normalizer seems to expect `model.version` not `model_version` so the model-version filter is dropped during normalization

lina_sre: tagging ingest-pipeline-bot — last deploy that touched filter-normalizer was 2026-03-01 02:11 UTC. there was a refactor for shorthand keys. ingest-pipeline-bot, any ingestion/backfill impacts?

ingest-pipeline-bot: Noted. No backlog processing currently. If filters are dropped we will still ingest events, but dashboard query could return larger/global buckets. No backfill scheduled.

support-bot: Created ticket CS-8952 and linked to this thread.

mike_prod: snippet from console service log around filter_normalizer:
```
WARN filter_normalizer - unknown key 'model_version' -> fallthrough
INFO query_builder - applied 1 filters (region) dropped 1 filters (model_version)
```
that explains why EU region shows up but model/version scoping is missing — chart aggregates across models in region or global if region also dropped in some cases

emma_support: customer also mentioned delayed metrics for the EU region yesterday (~3h lag). could the normalizer change cause metric indexing delay or mismatched buckets?

jordan_console: possible. if normalization removes filters we sometimes route to the global aggregation path which queries different time-bucket keys. that could manifest as missing/late data for scoped buckets.

lina_sre: plan: (1) quick compatibility patch to filter-normalizer to accept both `model_version` and `model.version` (2) add unit/regression test for shorthand mapping (3) canary patch to prod at 10% traffic then 100% if green. i'll freeze unrelated deploys until canary completes.

mike_prod: rolled compatibility patch to staging, verified UI now sends same payload and backend retains both region+model_version filters. staging query results match expected scoped counts. preparing canary PR.

emma_support: thanks — i'll update the customer with ETA ~2h for canary, will mention mitigation steps (use API with explicit model.version key as a temporary workaround).

jordan_console: note for follow-up: add telemetry alert when "filters_dropped" > 0.1% of requests in a 1h window.

lina_sre: agreed. also adding a data-reconciliation run for the last 24h to identify any buckets that may need backfill.

emma_support: appreciated. i'll keep CS-8952 updated and post customer note once canary is green. :thumbsup:
